sources.code_release: none found for either paper (arXiv page, GitHub, Hugging Face searched 2026-09-07)

shared_16bit_rows: identical in both papers for Llama-3.2-3B (10.7 / 66.2), Llama-3-8B (8.64 / 73.5), Qwen3-8B (9.71 / 71.6), Qwen3-14B (8.6 / 74.2), Qwen3-32B (7.6 / 75.2), including every per-task accuracy; they differ on Qwen3-4B (MosaicQuant 10.04 / 69.4, TwinQuant 13.7 / 66.8)

checkpoints.stated: 'LLaMA3 models (3B/8B) and Qwen3 models (4B/8B/14B/32B)'; no Hugging Face ids, no Base/post-trained statement in either paper
checkpoints.resolution: E23 gate evaluates Base and post-trained candidates and keeps the one whose 16-bit row reproduces

wikitext2_perplexity.stated: 'we also report the perplexity score on WikiText2'; nothing about split, context length, chunking or BOS
wikitext2_perplexity.note: Llama-3-8B at 8.64 is not the 2048-token non-overlapping convention (6.14 there, as BWLA arXiv 2605.00422 and TWLA arXiv 2606.13054 print), so the convention differs from QuaRot/GPTQ-style evaluation; candidates measured by the gate: non-overlapping 2048/4096 windows with one leading BOS, BOS-per-window (this repository), and lm-eval 'wikitext' word_perplexity (rolling, max_length 2048/4096)

calibration.stated: 'we randomly sample the 128 prompts from WikiText-2 dataset for calibration, each sentence with 2048 tokens' (both papers, following FlatQuant / SpinQuant)

weight_quantizer.mosaicquant: 'For the 4-bit setting, we adopt per-group and per-channel symmetric quantization for activations and weights, respectively' (C.1); RTN base plus sparse residual; GPTQ settings for the GPTQ/QuaRot/SpinQuant baselines unstated
weight_quantizer.twinquant: 'We apply group-wise quantization to both weights and activations, where each contiguous group of 128 elements shares one quantization scale' (5.1); symmetric per Eq. 1
weight_quantizer.status: stated (differs between the two papers: per-channel vs group-128 weights)

activation_quantizer.mosaicquant: per-group symmetric, group size not printed for W4A4 (W4A8 uses per-token dynamic)
activation_quantizer.status: partly stated; group size 128 assumed for MosaicQuant

kv_cache.stated: not mentioned in either paper (only QServe/COMET are cited as W4A8KV4/W4A4KV4 systems)
kv_cache.status: unstated; assumed 16-bit, so their W4A4 is W4A4KV16

zero_shot.stated: 'All accuracy metrics are tested on lm-eval'; version unstated; acc vs acc_norm unstated
zero_shot.status: tasks stated; version and metric unstated; the gate reports both acc and acc_norm per task and matches against the printed per-task rows

baseline_provenance.mosaicquant: 'For AWQ, FlatQuant, and QuaRot, we adopt the official PyTorch-based code and recommended W4A4/W4A8 configurations for each model' (C.1, speed section); accuracy provenance of the other baselines unstated

published_w4a4_rows.format: [WikiText-2 PPL, six-task mean]; per-task rows are in nar/e23_bridge.py PUBLISHED_16BIT and results/e23/published_per_task.json
published_w4a4_rows.note: QuaRot and SpinQuant differ between the two papers for the same model (re-runs, not copies), so each paper's W4A4 protocol differs even though the 16-bit rows are shared

decision_2026-09-07.target: TwinQuant only (user decision); MosaicQuant rows are recorded above for reference but not bridged
decision_2026-09-07.gate: the 16-bit reproduction gate (Step 2) was dropped at the user's request; our bf16 row is measured under our conventions and printed next to TwinQuant's 16-bit row

protocol_run.activations: group-128 symmetric int4, dynamic, all linear inputs ('symmetric_g128', 4.125 bits)
protocol_run.zero_shot: six tasks, zero-shot, pinned harness b954108c, acc_norm where defined
protocol_run.perplexity: WikiText-2 test, 146 windows of 2048 with BOS per window, fp32 NLL (E19/E22 convention)

decision_2026-09-08: E23 restricted to Qwen3-8B (user decision): the 14B and 32B bridge runs (jobs 144402, 144262) were cancelled after the 8B showed a bf16 reference 3.6 PPL above TwinQuant's under an unstated convention, a NAR k=8 row below bf16 on 144/146 windows, and a k=max row above Hadamard under the symmetric quantizer; a weight-only decomposition (job 144407) is attributing both before anything is written.
